To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pyruvatedecarboxylating enzyme pyruvate ferredoxin oxidoreducatse from the sulfate-reducer Desulfovibro africanus has been crystallized and that the crystal structure of this enzyme will be solved.
we have crystallized the PFOR from D. africanus and that these crystals diffract X-rays to 2. 3 A resolution.

we have crystallized and solved the three-dimensional structure of a pyruvic acid-ferredoxin reductase (PFPR) from Desulfovibrion africanus, which catalyzes the crucial energy-yield reaction of pyruvic acid decarboxylation in anaerobic bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural analysis of PFOR from D. africanus.
the structural and functional characterization of a pyruvic-oxidoreductase (EC 1.2.7.1).
the structural and functional characterization of enzymes involved in the metabolism of the anaerobic bacteria Desulfovibro africanus and Desulfovibrobacter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PFOR from D. africanus is the first PFOR for which crystals suitable for high-resolution X-ray diffraction studies have been obtained.
the crystallization of PFOR from D. africanus was achieved, and the crystallographic analysis is in progress.
the crystallographic studies of PFOR are still in an initial phase and the structural information available at this stage is very limited, although the preliminary results obtained are encouraging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to obtain crystals of a pyridine-nucleotide-independent pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, which is an essential enzyme in anaerobic metabolism.
, after a long period of unsuccessful crystallization attempts, crystals of a PFOR suitable for X-ray diffraction analysis have finally been obtained.
, for the first time, a crystallographic analysis has been initiated for the PFOR enzyme from D. africanus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of PEG and divalent metal ions in combination with a suitable crystallization buffer is an efficient way of crystallizing proteins.
PFOR crystallizes in a way that makes it amenable to X-ray analysis.
the use of divalent metal cation, together with polyethylene glycol, is a very effective way to crystallize PFOR.
